cards.explanation: The answer is Jerusalem. Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, reigns there twenty-five years (1 Kings 22:42). That's a long stretch on one throne, friends. I'm proud of everybody for being here.

The answer is his father Asa. The text says Jehoshaphat walked in all the ways of Asa and did not turn away from them (1 Kings 22:43). Not some of the ways, ALL of them. That's a son who stuck with the recipe.
The word is right. Jehoshaphat "…did what was right in the eyes of the LORD." (1 Kings 22:43). The LORD's eyes are the ones that count, and that's the report on him. A good report, friends!

The answer is True. The text says the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense on them (1 Kings 22:43). So a good report on the king comes with a "however." The Bible tells it straight, good and not-so-good side by side.

Jehoshaphat makes peace with him. The text says Jehoshaphat "…also made peace with the king of Israel." (1 Kings 22:44). Two kings, two kingdoms, and peace between them. That's one short verse, but it's a big deal.

The answer is False. The text says Jehoshaphat "…banished from the land the male shrine prostitutes who remained from the days of his father Asa." (1 Kings 22:46). So he cleared them out of the land. Good stuff, friends.
The answer is gold! Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold (1 Kings 22:48). That's a whole set of ships built to go get it. I can't even get my cookie boxes organized.

They're wrecked before they sail. The ships "…never set sail, because they were wrecked at Ezion-geber." (1 Kings 22:48). All that building, and they never left the harbor. I think that one hurt a little.
The answer is False. Ahaziah, son of Ahab, asks to sail his servants with Jehoshaphat's servants, and Jehoshaphat refuses (1 Kings 22:49). The request goes in, and the answer comes back no.
The answer is David! Jehoshaphat "…was buried with them in the city of his father David." (1 Kings 22:50). His son Jehoram took the throne after him. He rests with his fathers, in the same city.

The answer is True. The text says Ahaziah "…did evil in the sight of the LORD…" (1 Kings 22:52). He walked in the ways of his father and mother and of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin. This is a heavy part.

The answer is Baal. Ahaziah "…served and worshiped Baal, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger, just as his father had done." (1 Kings 22:53). It's a sad ending to the passage. Thank you for staying with it, friends.
